## Creating an example dataset
#Suppose we have  information about 10 students.
```{r}
Students<-data.frame(
  
  ID=1:10,
  
  Name=c("David","James","Divine","Jane","Kabayiza","Diane","Anitha","Nadia",
    "Keza","Johnson","Alice","John","Peter","Mary","Charles","Grace","Elia",
    "Elissa", "Aline","Arteta"),
  Sex= c("M","M","F","F","M","F","F","F","F","M","F","M","M","F","M","F","M",
  "M","F","M"),
  Age=c(19,20,21,18,25,30,29,20,25,40,50,19,20,21,27,25,33,34,32,20),
  Ass_Marks=c(1,27,29,11,18,19,26,21,22,20,28,25,23,17,30,13,15,24,21,22)
)
Students
```
#Creating other variables and add them in the dataset
#create first the variable list you want to include 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
Quiz_score=c(8,9,10,10,6,7,5,4,7,8,9,10,9,8,9,10,10,6,7,5)
Exam_score=c(29,12,18,30,35,38,37,39,33,32,31,24,30,22,21,7,36,36,20,17)
Students_scores <- Students %>% 
mutate(Quiz=Quiz_score,
       Exam=Exam_score,
       Total_score=Ass_Marks+Quiz_score+Exam_score)
  
Students_scores 
```
#Selecting Students aged 20years and above whose total score is at least 50marks
```{r}
library(dplyr)
Students1 <-Students_scores %>%
 filter(Age>=20,Total_score>=50)
Students1
```
#Inspecting the Students1.
```{r}
Grade_students <- Students_scores %>%
mutate(result=if_else(Total_score>=50,
                      'Pass','Fail'))
Grade_students
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
nrow(Grade_students)
```
```{r}
Grade_students %>%
count(result)
```
```{r}
#Counting the number of Male and Female(frequency)
library(dplyr)
Grade_students %>%
count(Sex) 
```
```{r}
"ggplot2" %in% rownames(installed.packages())
```





## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
